title: Oldhamia fossil trace from Chorrillos
dateKind: Geological period and separate collecting event recorded by Yale Peabody.
observation: Yale Peabody records a fossil trace assigned to Oldhamia from the Los Guachos Formation at Chorrillos in Salta Province, Argentina. The image caption is more specific than the genus field.
limit: A pattern on the surface and the animal that produced it are separate observations. The caption and taxon field have different levels of precision.
alt: A light stone face at an angle, with fine shallow marks and a dark background.
nearAction: Set the stop at the branching trace
near: The next carrier can find the same branching mark on the model. Its maker still has an empty label.
farAction: Open the caption beside the catalogue’s genus field
far: The image caption can be found beside the broader genus field. Readers can tell which wording came from which place.

title: Sallamys tooth from the Salla Beds
dateKind: Geological epoch and collecting month in the Yale Peabody record.
observation: This Yale Peabody lot from La Paz Department, Bolivia, contains an upper left tooth catalogued as Sallamys pascuali. Its particular position in the jaw is qualified in the specimen note.
limit: The record proposes a precise position. It leaves that placement open to later comparison.
alt: Small dark fossil tooth beside a written museum label and a ruled scale.
nearAction: Line up the surviving tooth with the adjustable stop
near: The stop can reproduce the single tooth’s position on the work tray, ready for a second look.
farAction: Keep the locator movable on the model jaw
far: The possible tooth position stays on a movable marker. A future comparison can shift it without losing the observation of the tooth.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
title: Megaoryzomys specimen from Isla Santa Cruz
dateKind: Collection date. The Smithsonian entry leaves geological age open.
observation: The Smithsonian’s record for this fossil places it on Isla Santa Cruz, Ecuador, and dates its collection to 28 July 1978. The accession includes the name Megaoryzomys curioi.
limit: Knowing when the collector recovered it leaves the age of the fossil unresolved.
alt: Brown fossil jaw with several teeth and a black and white scale.
nearAction: Set the collection slip at the place pin
near: A carrier can match Isla Santa Cruz to the collecting day and leave with the right record.
farAction: Add the separate open age strip
far: The geological age marker stays blank on its own rail. The collecting year cannot slide into that empty field.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
title: Poseidonamicus microslide from off Rio de Janeiro
dateKind: Geological epoch and recorded collecting date for this Smithsonian specimen.
observation: The Smithsonian lists this exact microslide from off Rio de Janeiro. Its external-view photograph shows a left adult female valve with a scale of 200 micrometres.
limit: The reference applies to this photographic view. An enlarged print can have a different paper size while retaining the same specimen scale.
alt: A magnified pale valve with a textured surface and a scale bar on a black background.
nearAction: Match one divider to the scale bar and the outer edge
near: The carrier repeats the same small distance on the enlargement and records it in micrometres.
farAction: Check the scale again after the larger print is mounted
far: The audience sees a longer printed line for the same reference distance. Both scale bars stay by their own views.

title: 9 de Julio, the Met’s 1895 albumen card
dateKind: The Met’s date for this albumen card.
observation: The Met lists this 3.8 by 6.7 cm albumen card in a commercial series. The caption names the ship 9 de Julio and the Republic of Argentina.
limit: The dated card shows a published image of the vessel. It gives neither the ship’s dimensions nor its performance.
alt: Small brown albumen card with a side view of a ship and a floor of lettering.
nearAction: Set the little paper gauge to 3.8 by 6.7 cm
near: The next carrier can fit the same paper profile beside the catalogue card without guessing about the vessel.
farAction: Move the vessel caption to the separate pictured-subject slot
far: The second reader sees two roles. The dimensions describe the card and the pictured subject has only a name.

title: Pouch (Bolsa) from Haurina
dateKind: Approximate time of making given by the Cleveland Museum for this Haurina pouch.
observation: The Cleveland Museum locates this pouch in Haurina, Bolivia. It records wool, glass beads and sequins, and gives overall dimensions of 25.5 by 36.3 cm.
limit: The outside measurements leave the pouch’s actual capacity and maker open.
alt: Patterned pouch with many narrow stripes in red and cream and a long strap above.
nearAction: Set the outer profile gauge to the measured sides
near: The reader can compare the envelope against the outside size before any other check.
farAction: Leave the inside measure on its empty stop
far: Readers can try the external profile and see where a separate capacity measurement would have to go.

title: Pouch (Bolsa) from Choclla
dateKind: Approximate time of making given by the Cleveland Museum for this Choclla pouch.
observation: The Cleveland Museum gives this wool pouch from Choclla, Bolivia, overall dimensions of 26.7 by 31.2 cm. Its catalogue number is 1947.191.
limit: Several catalogue entries use the title Pouch. The named place and accession distinguish these measurements.
alt: Dark red patterned pouch with a strap that loops above it.
nearAction: Seat the profile measure beside the 1947.191 tab
near: The narrow stand keeps the Choclla number with this profile.
farAction: Lay two empty source slots beside the similar titles
far: Readers can see why a title alone cannot let them swap dimensions from a separately catalogued pouch.

title: Paraguayan lace collar, 54.94.1
dateKind: The Met’s making date for this individual collar.
observation: The Met gives this Paraguayan collar an overall length of 90.2 cm and identifies the fibre as cotton with a question mark.
limit: The length is recorded. The catalogue qualifies the fibre. The outline alone leaves maker and exact fibre uncertain.
alt: Long pale lace strip with an open repeating pattern and pointed end.
nearAction: Set the length stop against the line for 90.2 cm
near: The small stand shows a reader where length begins and ends.
farAction: Clip the fibre qualifier separately from the length mark
far: The new work surface keeps the question mark where a materials checker can see it without changing the length.

title: Wat-Sa-Pua, Met 89.4.685
dateKind: Century given in the Met’s collection record.
observation: The Met catalogues this instrument with an historic Demerara attribution in what is now Guyana. It records bone, wool and wax and dimensions of 3.9 cm in diameter and 28 cm in length.
limit: The dimensions and listed materials describe this object. They do not establish how it sounded, a named maker or every musical use.
alt: Long pale instrument against a plain background, with a dark opening at one end.
nearAction: Fit the short diameter guide across the model outline
near: The carrier can reproduce a size comparison without claiming to reproduce a sound.
farAction: Set the longer stop on its own axis and leave the sound space blank
far: A pair of readers can check which measurement is across and which is along, with sound still an open question.

title: Tropical Scenery, Cathedral, Cartagena
dateKind: Date given for John Moran’s albumen silver print.
observation: The Met identifies John Moran as the photographer. It lists an image of 20 by 27.6 cm on a larger mount of 30.5 by 38.1 cm. The print names Cartagena.
limit: The mount and image have different edges. The published view leaves activity beyond the camera’s frame open.
alt: Brown-toned photograph of a long church building and adjacent frontage facing a street.
nearAction: Set the small stop at the photograph’s own edge
near: The narrow rail lets two visitors in turn check the edge of the actual view.
farAction: Slide back the paper surround to mark the separate mount
far: The public work surface shows both perimeters. A reader can explain which size describes which part.

title: José Negretti’s [Mining Site Chincha Islands, Lima]
dateKind: The Met’s approximate date range for this photographic print.
observation: The Met credits José Negretti and uses a bracketed site title. The photograph is an albumen silver print with an image of 5.4 by 8.6 cm and a mount of 6.4 by 10.0 cm.
limit: The print gives a view from one position. It cannot provide each worker’s account or identify everything beyond the frame.
alt: Small photographic view of a steep working slope on a mount with a coloured border.
nearAction: Line the aperture up with the small framed view
near: The carrier can point out exactly where the view ends and leave the work beyond it open.
farAction: Put the credited title and an open testimony pocket beside the image
far: Readers can follow the exact print and see where another record might describe work beyond the frame.

title: Valparaiso, the Met’s City Flags card
dateKind: Date assigned to this commercial colour lithograph.
observation: The Met catalogues this 7 by 3.8 cm card as a commercial print in Allen & Ginter’s City Flags series. The card title names Valparaíso in Chile.
limit: The commercial series depicts a banner. The record does not establish how official it was or who used it.
alt: Small colour print with flag graphics above a tiny waterfront view.
nearAction: Fit the small viewer to the 7 by 3.8 cm sheet
near: The narrow stand gives the reader the size of this printed card.
farAction: Expose the publisher line beside the banner image
far: Another reader can check which claim comes from a commercial series and keep the official-status field open.

title: Awl punch catalogued from Tierra del Fuego
dateKind: The Met’s wide period for this exact catalogue object.
observation: The Met lists a 26.7 cm width for this awl punch from Tierra del Fuego, Argentina, and names whalebone and ivory as its materials.
limit: The broad date and named materials leave the person who made it and their exact technique open.
alt: A long slender pale worked object with a slightly curving outline.
nearAction: Place the long silhouette under the paper measure
near: A visitor can check the extent of the outline without handling or trying to make the historical object.
farAction: Frame both printed ends and keep the catalogue’s broad date range
far: The public stand supports a dimension check and keeps the open interval of making in view.

title: Chorrera bowl, Met 1991.436.2
dateKind: The Met’s date range for this ceramic object.
observation: The Met identifies this as a ceramic bowl made in the Chorrera tradition of Ecuador. Its entry gives three dimensions, 23.5, 17.8 and 5.7 cm.
limit: The catalogue dimensions describe the bowl’s extent. Its contents, capacity and a particular person’s use need other evidence.
alt: Brown-red ceramic bowl seen obliquely, with a shallow curving interior.
nearAction: Set an outer edge stop to the larger recorded span
near: The next carrier can repeat one exact size check in the narrow lane.
farAction: Set another support for the depth and leave an open capacity slot
far: The silhouette can be checked along two axes. The space for an inside measure stays open.

title: Poivre d’inde, the Cleveland 1771 engraving
dateKind: The date assigned to this particular hand-coloured printed plate.
observation: The Cleveland Museum records this hand-coloured engraving as plate 55 in a series on insects of Suriname and Europe. Its catalogue credits Maria Sibylla Merian, whose lifetime ended before the plate date.
limit: The edition date describes the print. It cannot date every observation in the work or every coloured impression.
alt: Hand-coloured print of a leafy branch with several coloured insects.
nearAction: Line the picture edge up with the 1771 print slip
near: The narrow rail preserves when the displayed plate was dated.
farAction: Place artist and printed plate on separate dated supports
far: Readers can see the earlier artist credit and the later edition together without putting observation and printing on one date.

title: Spinning Whorl, CMA 1921.1541
dateKind: The Cleveland Museum’s upper bound for the date of making.
observation: The Cleveland Museum records this Colombian red-ware whorl with a diameter of 4.8 cm and overall dimension of 2.6 cm.
limit: An upper date bound leaves the precise year open. The diameter describes this piece and cannot supply a working speed.
alt: Round red-brown piece with concentric decoration and a hole at the top.
nearAction: Place a paper ring around the 4.8 cm outer diameter
near: The stand shows how to compare the outer size without making a claim about speed.
farAction: Keep the overall dimension on a separate stop beside the date bound
far: Both recorded dimensions remain distinguishable. The date slip ends at a bound and keeps the earlier end open.

title: Diatom slide from Puerto Cabello
dateKind: Month of collection recorded by Naturalis for RGM.966969.
observation: Naturalis’s occurrence record identifies Bacillariophyceae from Puerto Cabello, Venezuela, and uses March 1896 as the collecting month. The image shows a slide and its labels.
limit: A photograph of the slide label can place the record. It does not supply a view of every cell or a species identification.
alt: Long greenish microscope slide with written labels and a small round mount.
nearAction: Align the collection strip with the slide label
near: The carrier keeps the month and named place with the same slide.
farAction: Set a second empty support for an actual microscope view
far: The workshop can verify the slide label immediately and reserve a separate check for the cells.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
title: Part and counterpart of a Paleosquilla fossil
dateKind: Geological period and collecting date in the Smithsonian record.
observation: This Smithsonian holotype from the Simití Formation in Antioquia, Colombia, is catalogued as Paleosquilla. The museum identifies the photograph’s two sides as part and counterpart.
limit: The photograph shows two facing pieces of the record. Counting those as two animals would change the observation.
alt: Two rounded fossil bearing stone pieces next to a horizontal scale.
nearAction: Fit one face against the known profile support
near: The next carrier can reproduce one side’s outline without assigning a body count.
farAction: Reunite the part and counterpart on their matching supports
far: The other reader can compare matching faces and preserve the one accession for the pair.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
title: Ostracode image from Chimbote, USNM PAL 247790
dateKind: Year of collection given by the Smithsonian. Geological age is unstated in the linked record.
observation: The Smithsonian places this accession at Chimbote, Peru. The chosen external valve image gives a 200-micrometre scale. Its image caption leaves genus and species undetermined.
limit: The photograph permits a length comparison for this view. It does not settle the biological identification.
alt: Pale oval valve against black, with an accession label and bright scale.
nearAction: Re-centre the bar against the outer curve of the valve
near: The carrier can compare this valve outline to the same fixed scale.
farAction: Set its qualified identification apart from the scale check
far: The new surface lets a reader measure a feature while leaving the name field as unresolved as the image caption.

title: Glossotherium skull from Chimborazo Province
dateKind: Geological period and collection date in the Yale Peabody record.
observation: Yale Peabody records a skull from Chimborazo Province, Ecuador. The photograph identifies it as Glossotherium sp. and shows a specimen scale.
limit: The recorded skull and photographed scale leave the dimensions of the whole animal and exact species open.
alt: Large fossil skull in a tray, with labels and a black and white scale bar.
nearAction: Align the skull outline with the photographed reference
near: The carrier can read the preserved extent on the tray sketch without estimating the whole animal.
farAction: Add the separate blank for species and the collected date
far: Readers can inspect the skull’s scale and keep the known date of collection from filling the open identification field.

title: Schizaea pennula sheet north of Zanderij
dateKind: Collection day in the Yale Peabody herbarium record.
observation: The Yale Peabody record for this sheet names Rolla M. Tryon and the road to Hanover north of Zanderij, Suriname. The preserved specimen is catalogued as Schizaea pennula.
limit: A labelled specimen documents a particular collection. It cannot give the plant’s range or abundance along every part of the road.
alt: Two dry branching plant samples with labels mounted on one sheet.
nearAction: Set the locality tab beside the preserved sample outline
near: A later runner can follow the proper place description attached to the sheet.
farAction: Keep an open blank for repeated observations along the road
far: Visitors can point to one collection place and see why it cannot substitute for a roadside survey.

title: Hymenophyllum secundum sheet from Borja Bay
dateKind: Collection day for this Chilean herbarium specimen. The separate Yale image dates to 2010.
observation: Yale Peabody records a specimen of Hymenophyllum secundum collected at Borja Bay, Chile, on 2 January 1888. The photograph identifies a digital image made by the museum’s botany division in 2010.
limit: The dates refer to different acts. One records the collection event and one the image of its sheet.
alt: A narrow, dried branching specimen mounted on a museum sheet.
nearAction: Keep the collecting date clipped beside the specimen position
near: A reader can find the specific collecting day without confusing it with the age of the photograph.
farAction: Add the digital image slip to a different dated support
far: The two dated statements remain visible together while each keeps its own referent.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, U.S. National Herbarium
title: Toulicia plant sheet collected at Cerro Corá
dateKind: Collection date in the U.S. National Herbarium record.
observation: The U.S. National Herbarium records Toulicia tomentosa from near a monument in Parque Nacional Cerro Corá, Paraguay. The catalogue names W. D. Stevens, O. Montiel J., C. Davidson, and S. Christoph as collectors.
limit: The named landmark identifies a specific collection place near a monument. It does not map plant distribution across the park.
alt: Pressed woody plant material and several leaves, labels and a scale strip.
nearAction: Seat the named landmark with the accession tab
near: The walker can tie the preserved collection to one description of place.
farAction: Add a support for the four named collectors beside the location note
far: Readers can compare where the record comes from and whose collecting work it credits.

institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, U.S. National Herbarium
title: Trichocline sheet from Paso Ataques
dateKind: Collection day in the U.S. National Herbarium record.
observation: The U.S. National Herbarium labels this Trichocline maxima collection from Paso Ataques, Tranqueras, Uruguay. It names E. Pasini, F. Torchelsen, and E. Hayden, and gives field number 1019.
limit: The collectors’ field number and the institutional accession have different roles. Neither means there were 1019 plants.
alt: One pressed plant on a pale sheet with leaves spread out around a centre and labels below.
nearAction: Match the field number on the practice sheet to the location register
near: The narrow check gives the carrier one retrievable collection event.
farAction: Set the institutional accession at its own stop and link the two references
far: The reader can find both records and see that their numbers identify records instead of measuring abundance.
